ideas.idea: RMSNorm fused into the next GEMM's A-load (+ bias/residual epilogue)
ideas.reason: The board's QKV/gate/up calls are served by three different GEMM bodies with their own staging: NVIDIA's packed kpack body (_kpack_run, IDN_GEMM_NV_STEP_KPACK default on for stepped-down calls), AMD's identical_gemm_mfma16_kernel, and the scalar identical_gemm_tuned_kernel fallback, all in gemm/checks/gemm_identical.mojo which L10 (dedupe) and L12 (ozaki) are editing. A prologue needs a comptime A-transform plus two kernel args (rstd, gamma) in each body; bits stay equal because A_eff = ftz(w*ftz(x*rstd)) is the incumbent S3/S4 value. Stats kernel (S1/S2) stays serial per row; stage x through shared memory for coalescing. Residual epilogue must go into the fold kernel for GROUP/split launches. Existing partial routes: MOJOLEARN_FUSE_RESIDUAL1_NORM2 (residual+norm2 on NV/AMD), NN25/NI25 norm geometry arms. Owed after L10/L12 merge.

Contract gemm.fp32.v1 7.1 forbids splitting a leaf (128 k), so the finest deterministic unit is (tile, leaf); stream-K at that grain is leaf split-K, which exists: DEVIATION 2595 ksplit/ksplit_leaf arms, PLAN_SPLIT_* plans, the tile step-down (GEMM_TILE_MIN_BLOCKS) and NN10 cost plan. Sub-leaf stream-K would carry the accumulator serially between CTAs (no parallelism). A per-device fill rule over (tile, leaf-split) is NN10's job.

ideas.idea: Persistent chunked Mamba2/Mamba3 SSD at batch 1
ideas.reason: Mamba2 (ssd_minimal.ssd_forward) and Mamba3 (mamba3_siso) do not launch per chunk: the chunk-state pass is one kernel per call, parallel over (h,p,n) cells, serial over chunks. A persistent version would fuse the ~10 (M2) / ~25 (M3) launches with decoupled look-back over chunk states in fixed chunk order; bits unchanged if each stage keeps its fold. Large kernel, measured launch share unknown; Mamba-1 (the real per-window/under-filled case) is built as m1_persistent_scan.

ideas.idea: Split-KV attention on the v1 profile / decode lanes
ideas.reason: v1 S17 denominator and S19 value sum are serial ascending chains over all keys (IDENTICAL_TRANSFORMER_CONTRACT 5.3), so any KV split is a new profile; the summary-tree profile NN20 is the one where a split is bit-free, so split-KV is built on NN20. Board decode/*-infer lanes are CPU host bindings and never GPU-timed.
